name: main
description: The landmark holding what the page is actually for, once the furniture around it is taken away. The third of the three landmarks a page frames itself with, from the same practice page banner and contentinfo are adopted from and for the same reason, since landmarks are a practice and not a widget. One per page, so no name is required: a reader jumping by landmark reaches it by its role. It carries one requirement the other two do not, and it is the whole reason a skip link works at all: the region has to be focusable programmatically, because sending focus to a container the platform will not focus leaves the focus where it was and the reader lands nowhere.

requires.roles.element: main (native main at the top level of the document, or role=main when main cannot be used)
requires.focus.target: the landmark is programmatically focusable, so an anchor pointing at it moves focus into it rather than only scrolling to it
